records.reason: The original delegation instruction leaves the access boundary unspecified. sources.title: About Azure Key Vault certificate renewal

proposedEdits.after: Configure certificate lifetime actions and renewal for the supported integrated certificate authorities, DigiCert and GlobalSign. For certificates issued by nonintegrated authorities, configure expiry notifications and an external or manual issuance/import workflow that creates the replacement certificate version. sources.title: How to Use Named Values in Azure API Management policies

proposedEdits.after: Reference a Key Vault secret from the named value using an API Management managed identity with the required secret-read permissions. Use a versionless secret identifier for automatic refresh, and verify access after rotation; the documented refresh interval is up to four hours. This integration is not available for workspace named values. Restrict policy-editing and request-tracing access because storing the source secret in Key Vault does not prevent authorized API Management features from exposing its resolved value.

querySemanticsConcerns: A Key Vault reference or managed identity in ARG is not proof of successful secret retrieval, refresh, or safe policy/tracing permissions. Do not retrieve resolved secret values in a query or report.
remainingLimitations: The fetched firewall guidance requires the system-assigned identity for the documented trusted-service firewall scenario; this proposal does not assert that every identity/network combination works. Secret size bounds and tier/network configuration still require deployment-specific checks.

before.title: Use Azure Key Vault to store TLS certificates
before.description: Application Gateway can be integrated with Key Vault. This provides stronger security, easier separation of roles and responsibilities, support for managed certificates, and an easier certificate renewal and rotation process.

records.reason: Current Application Gateway documentation limits the integration to v2 and identifies concrete certificate, identity, rotation and failure conditions missing from the original general recommendation. proposedEdits.before: Use Azure Key Vault to store TLS certificates
proposedEdits.after: Use Azure Key Vault certificates for Application Gateway v2 HTTPS listeners.

proposedEdits.before: Application Gateway can be integrated with Key Vault. This provides stronger security, easier separation of roles and responsibilities, support for managed certificates, and an easier certificate renewal and rotation process.
proposedEdits.after: Use an enabled software-backed PFX certificate with an exportable private key, and reference its Key Vault secret through a user-assigned managed identity with the required secret-read permission. Prefer a versionless secret identifier so Application Gateway can retrieve renewed versions during its four-hour polling cycle. Verify Key Vault network reachability and monitor access failures, because loss of certificate access can disable the listener. HSM-backed certificates are not supported by this integration.
